title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: ROZ STEPS IN
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Roz Tate, a parking garage cashier in Baltimore, Maryland.
For twenty-two years, she sat in a little glass booth.
Then the old boxing gym across the street needed a new roof.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BOOTH
segments.quote: I don't have to be what you want me to be. I'm free to be what I want.
segments.author: Muhammad Ali
lines: Coach Earl, seventy-four, needed twenty thousand dollars for that roof, so he planned a charity fight night. Headgear, three short rounds.
Roz said, put me down. Her sister Denise laughed. You're forty-nine. You sit in a box.
But on the gym wall hung an old poster of Muhammad Ali:
I don't have to be what you want me to be. I'm free to be what I want.
Roz signed her name in big letters.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FIRST PUNCH
segments.quote: Everybody has plans until they get hit for the first time.
segments.author: Mike Tyson
lines: Roz had a plan. She would dance, like Ali.
In her first practice round, a retired mail carrier named Gloria tapped her right on the headgear.
The plan left the building. Earl laughed and quoted Mike Tyson:
Everybody has plans until they get hit for the first time.
New plan. Hands up. Chin down. Breathe.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: HER OWN STYLE
segments.quote: Absorb what is useful, reject what is useless and add what is essentially your own.
segments.author: Bruce Lee
lines: She couldn't float like the famous fighters. Then she read a note on the mirror, from Bruce Lee:
Absorb what is useful, reject what is useless and add what is essentially your own.
What was her own? Twenty-two years of patience, and counting change.
So Roz learned to wait, count, and make you pay.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SORE WEEK
segments.quote: The most certain sign of wisdom is cheerfulness.
segments.author: Michel de Montaigne
lines: Week three, everything hurt. Even her eyebrows.
She tripped on the jump rope in front of six firefighters, and wanted to quit.
Then she remembered Montaigne, an old French writer:
The most certain sign of wisdom is cheerfulness.
So Roz took a bow. They clapped. She came back the next day, laughing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: BIG TINA
segments.quote: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
segments.author: Sun Tzu
lines: Her opponent was Big Tina, a firefighter six inches taller.
Earl handed her a thin book by Sun Tzu, a Chinese general:
If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
When Tina got tired, she dropped her left hand. And Roz faded in round two.
So she ran the garage stairs every lunch break.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: FIGHT NIGHT
segments.quote: He can run, but he can't hide.
segments.author: Joe Louis
lines: Fight night, three hundred people came. Denise held up a sign.
In round three, Tina started dancing away. Roz thought of the great Joe Louis:
He can run, but he can't hide.
Roz kept coming, and tapped that open left side.
A draw. Twenty-three thousand dollars. New roof.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be free. Adjust. Be yourself. Laugh. Know yourself. Keep coming.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Choose who you are. Make a new plan. Use what's yours. Laugh when it hurts. Know yourself. Keep coming.
I tried the jump rope once. The rope won.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
